description:
We are Machine Without Learning, a student team passionate about AI, Data Science, and space exploration.

For NASA Space Apps 2026, we use NASA open data, machine learning, and statistics to explore Earth's environmental changes.

We welcome curious people interested in AI/ML, data analysis, and Earth science.
summary:
EarthTrend Explorer is a scientifically grounded climate intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge: "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" Leveraging 43 years (1981–2023) of authentic NASA POWER (MERRA-2) atmospheric reanalysis records across Egyptian climate regimes—Greater Cairo, Alexandria, and Aswan—the platform functions as a statistical laboratory detecting multi-decadal warming, abrupt hydrologic breaks, and future climate anomalies.

Directly addressing the challenge, EarthTrend Explorer rigorously investigates: what is changing, where, by how much, and with what statistical confidence? It couples robust non-parametric trend estimators (Theil-Sen slope, Mann-Kendall, Hamed-Rao serial autocorrelation corrections, and Pettitt regime-shift detection) with a multi-scalar drought engine (SPI) and a forward-looking predictive engine (Holt-Winters ETS, SARIMAX) verified via expanding-window backtesting and newly released 2024 observations.

This tool is critical because climate adaptation in water-stressed regions demands transparent, physically guarded evidence rather than unverified black-box claims. By uncovering steady warming (+0.26 to +0.43 °C/decade), an abrupt 2015 rainfall shift (+181% to +266%), and a tripling of compound hot-dry months, EarthTrend Explorer transforms authentic NASA Earth observations into actionable, uncertainty-quantified insight for regional resilience.
details:
EarthTrend Explorer

1. What does the project do?

EarthTrend Explorer is an interactive platform for analyzing climate changes in Egypt using real NASA data.

It studies 43 years of climate data (1981–2023) across three different regions in Egypt:

  • Greater Cairo: Urban climate.
  • Alexandria: Mediterranean coastal climate.
  • Aswan: Hot and dry desert climate.

The platform works through four main steps:

  1. Data Collection: Collects monthly temperature and rainfall data from NASA and prepares it for analysis.
  2. Climate Trend Analysis: Uses statistical methods to identify whether temperatures and rainfall are increasing or decreasing over time.
  3. Climate Anomaly Detection: Detects unusual weather patterns, sudden changes in rainfall, and drought conditions.
  4. Climate Forecasting: Uses different time-series models to predict climate conditions for the next 12 months.

2. What are its main benefits?

  • Provides reliable, long-term climate analysis based on real NASA observations.
  • Shows whether climate trends are statistically significant.
  • Helps identify unusual climate events and potential drought conditions.
  • Provides future climate predictions with uncertainty ranges.
  • Handles the special challenges of dry regions, especially Aswan, where rainfall is extremely rare.
  • Includes 71 automated tests, all passing, to check the reliability of the system.

3. What is the expected impact?

The project aims to make climate data easier to understand and use.

It provides insights into how climate conditions have changed across different Egyptian regions and how they might change in the future.

These insights could support research, agricultural planning, and water-resource management, especially in areas affected by water scarcity.

4. What technologies did we use?

  • Programming Language: Python 3.10+
  • Data Processing: Pandas and NumPy
  • Scientific Calculations: SciPy
  • Statistical Analysis: Statsmodels and PyMannKendall
  • Climate Data: NASA POWER API and MERRA-2
  • Data Visualization: Plotly
  • User Interface: Streamlit
  • Testing: Pytest and Streamlit AppTest

5. What makes the project creative?

  • Forecasting Model Competition: Instead of choosing one forecasting model, we compare three different models using historical data and select the one that performs best.
  • 2024 Reality Check: We compare our predictions with actual NASA observations from 2024 to evaluate how accurate the forecasts were.
  • Regional Climate Comparison: We investigate whether temperature trends are different between Upper Egypt and northern coastal regions.
  • Advanced Statistical Analysis: We use several statistical methods to detect long-term trends, sudden climate changes, and drought conditions.

6. What challenges did our team consider?

  • Understanding NASA Data: We carefully checked what each NASA climate variable represents to avoid incorrect calculations or interpretations.
  • Limited Rainfall in Aswan: Since Aswan has very little rainfall, standard drought measurements may not always work reliably. We added special checks to handle this problem.
  • Data Accuracy: We checked the data for missing values and ensured that monthly observations were complete.
  • Forecast Reliability: We tested different models using historical data instead of assuming that one model would always perform best.
  • Scientific Transparency: We made sure to distinguish between statistical relationships and actual physical causes. We also avoided generating or inventing scientific data using AI.
